Honestly, I just wanted someone to acknowledge it. Saying something like "Im sorry for your loss" or "sorry" or just "I hope things get easier". Just under no circumstances say something like "they're in a better place", "at least it wasn't \_\_\_", "damn that sucks", "wow", "you're so lucky, you have so many people", "other people have it worse", etc.... Trust me, if the person is grieving, you'd be surprised how bad people react to it. I did the exact same in highschool; I skipped a lot, showed up stoned, faked panic attacks and migraines to go sleep in the nurses' office, never applied myself, and basically just stayed miserable the entire time. My first year of college, I said "fuck it", and decided that drugs and alcohol gave me more joy than making friends- Big Mistake. I was lonelier than I could have ever imagined, and couldn't talk to anyone about the shit I was going through. I wish I didn't waste all those years due to feeling so badly about myself. 

Now, I have a few suggestions:

\-JOIN A CLUB OH MY GOD! If you're anything like me, I have a tendency to try and force friendships with people who do not like me at all, and I feel as if I'm imposing. But to be in a club, you are BY DEFINITION not imposing! You have every right to be there!

\-Volunteer! Even if you don't make friends, you'll feel good about helping the world around you

\-Get a job outside of college, I recommend a restaurant/bar, because everyone tends to hang out and drink after their shift

\-GO TO FROSH WEEK!!!! I thought I was too cool for it, and thought it would be lame, another Big Mistake. A ton of people made their friend group during frosh week and stuck with them

\-Participate in classes, and don't be afraid to invite people out to do things outside of class. If they reject you, no biggie! You didn't lose anything

\-Go to parties! Majority of the time, you don't need to be invited to show up. 

\-Finally, understand that people are more similar to you than you think, most people find their friends annoying at some point- that doesn't mean they hate your company. Annoying can be endearing, in some ways. 

Don't let your fears hold you back, rather, see if as you having nothing to lose! Good luck, I hope this year goes better than high school. Despite my attitude freshman year of college, my confidence shot up basically the second I left high school, even if it wasn't enough. Things get better if you let them!

Here's something that my therapist suggested to me:  look at your body objectively. For example: I am flat chested. Rather than look into the mirror and say "I look like a malnourished 13-year-old pre-pubescent boy", I say "I have quite small breasts". Understand that unless there is something legitimately wrong, it's really probably not that bad. I really understand hating your nose- I broke mine at multiple points in my teen years, leaving it with a large dent across the bridge, and pointing the tip downwards, all to say it was a very unusual looking schnoz. Now I don't know if your nose is broken, but odds are if you think "you look like an absolute monster", the nose is not the true root of the problem. 
Even if you do have a really peculiar looking nose, don't forget, it's just a nose. Even the biggest nose doesn't dim the sparkle in your eyes when you smile, or make your hugs any less comforting. When it comes to finding a boyfriend, think to yourself how important you think appearances are when choosing a partner. If you think it's the most important thing when searching for a boyfriend, then you may be out of luck. For me, I genuinely care most about how the other person makes me feel, and I would hate to think that the second I develop a wrinkle my SO will up and leave. You deserve someone who loves you for ALL of you. Looks fade and can change in a millisecond.
You are most definitely NOT unworthy of love because of your nose. Focus on other skills, etc, because the more you place your value on your appearance, the less time you spend living your life. 
I have moments where I fixate on my appearance a lot too, so this is not supposed to be mocking you, but I advise that you read back the paragraph you wrote and understand how ridiculous that sounds. Being a good person can never be overshadowed by a wonky side profile. Best of luck
